description: Baeza-Yates et al. (1999) used Kolmogorov complexity to derive upper bounds on expected LCS. A common subsequence provides a compressed description of one string given the other. Since random strings are incompressible, this limits LCS length. Tighter incompressibility arguments with refined conditional complexity could improve the upper bound.
mathematical_formalization: For random binary strings x,y of length n: K(x|y) >= n - O(log n). An LCS of length ell allows encoding x given y and the LCS in n - ell + O(ell * log(n/ell)) bits. Therefore ell/n <= c where c satisfies c*log(1/c) + (1-c)*log(1/(1-c)) >= c.
implementation_hypothesis: Refine the encoding scheme by exploiting the monotone lattice path structure of optimal alignments. Each improvement in encoding tightens the upper bound.
experiment_seed: Implement encoding/decoding scheme for n=20. For each pair, compute description length. Average over random pairs gives upper bound.
